# Generated by scripts/import.mjs from forgecycle 0.5.3. Do not edit.
title: "Dashboard"
description: "The local, read-only dashboard served by forgecycle serve."
sidebar:
  order: 5
---

Every command invoked inside a Git project writes a private operation
journal under the Git common directory, and `forgecycle serve` renders it as
a local, read-only dashboard (`--open` launches it in your browser) headed
with the project name. It listens on `127.0.0.1`; `--listen 0.0.0.0` lets
other machines on a trusted network open it over plain HTTP, and shows a QR
code of the network URL in the terminal and in the dashboard so a phone can
open it by scanning. `--public-url https://forge.example.com` (or a bare
domain) names the address behind a reverse proxy or DNS name, and the QR code
and share dialog offer it instead. The dashboard always offers a share dialog
that copies its URL with the access token; `--no-auth` drops the token, so
anyone who can reach the dashboard can read it. On a phone it opens on a "Now" summary (what needs
you, which agents are running, what just finished), shows one pane at a
time with the views in a bottom tab bar, and can be added to the home
screen. Its left panel is the planned work as a tree: each
plan with its decomposition and tasks, each task with its Planner, Builder,
and Reviewer turns, and standalone task runs. Selecting a turn opens that
agent on the right: what it concluded, what it read and wrote, its tests and
findings (a Reviewer's results next to what the Builder reported), its live
activity, the diff of a Builder turn, its evidence files, and the stored
handoff. Selecting a task shows its Markdown file (for a task run, the
snapshot its agents read). A task run shows its stop, next command, resume
target, and quota cooldowns. Its "Needs attention" list shows every run waiting for you, and
opt-in browser notifications announce each new stop while a dashboard tab is
open. Its "Notifications" view lists every stop that needed you and which
command resolved it; the run commands record it, so it includes stops from
while no dashboard was running. A "Commands" view lists the command
history, and a "Candidates" view shows each candidate's quality figures; the
left panel collapses to give the selected item the full width. `forgecycle observe --summary`
prints per-candidate quality figures: first-pass validity, repairs,
normalizations, quota cooldowns, and mean duration. See
[Observability](/documentation/guides/observability/) for storage, privacy, and adapter
capability details.
